hints.S40_A1: They LINED UP AT THE STARTING LINE, EAGER for the RELAY RACE to begin. Ask: which verb means to take an active part in something? 'Withdraw' and 'cancel' would empty the track before the whistle.
hints.S40_A2: It is the FINAL QUARTER, so the coach wants their EFFORTS to grow, not shrink. Ask: which verb means to increase something to twice as much? 'Reduce' and 'abandon' would hand the game away.
hints.S40_A3: They are at the STARTING BLOCKS, WAITING FOR THE STARTER'S PISTOL - muscles tight, ready to burst forward. Ask: which adjective describes a body wound up like a spring? 'Relaxed' and 'sleeping' say the opposite.
hints.S40_A4: They kept ENCOURAGING THEIR TEAMMATES EVEN AFTER FALLING BEHIND - losing did not make them mean. Ask: which noun names fair, generous behaviour in sport? Every other choice names a fault.
hints.S40_A5: The ANCHOR RUNNER took the BATON and SPRINTED THE FINAL LEG to win. Ask: which verb means to grab something firmly and quickly? 'Dropped' would lose the race, and 'studied' would stop it dead.
hints.S40_B1: HAS is already sitting in the sentence, waiting for its partner, and THREE YEARS IN A ROW reaches right up to today. Ask: after 'has', which form follows - plain, -s, -ing, or a past participle?
hints.S40_B2: THE SKY SUDDENLY TURNED DARK - a sharp event that cut into something already under way. Ask: which choice shows an action in progress in the past? A plain past verb would only report a finished job.
hints.S40_B3: THAN pits the RELAY against a SOLO 100M SPRINT - two events, not many. Ask: comparative or superlative? DEMANDING is long, so it needs a helper word, never an -er ending. 'Very' cannot pair with 'than'.
hints.S40_B4: Two past moments: the STRETCHES finished first, and only afterwards did THE FIRST EVENT start. Ask: which form shows the earlier of two past actions? BY THE TIME is the phrase that demands it.
hints.S40_B5: ENERGY cannot be counted - you never say 'three energies'. Ask: which word partners an uncountable noun after that GRUELLING MORNING SESSION? 'Few', 'many' and 'a few' all need countable things.
hints.S40_B6: A tag copies whichever helping verb runs the statement, and this statement ends with ANNOUNCED YET - a present perfect in negative form. Ask: after a negative statement, does its tag turn positive or stay negative?
hints.S40_B7: The GOLD MEDAL cannot win anything - BY A STUDENT FROM CLASS 3C tells you who acted, and THIS MORNING places it in past time. Ask: which choice is passive and past? Passive = a form of 'be' + past participle.
hints.S40_B8: A reported order sits here: TOLD THE STUDENTS what they must never do IN THE SUN WITHOUT DRINKING WATER. Ask: which verb form follows 'told' + person? And does a negative word come before that infinitive, or inside it?
hints.S40_C1: ENJOYS decides it: this verb is always followed by an -ing form, never by an infinitive. Ask: do you say 'enjoy to swim' or 'enjoy swimming'? Copy that shape here - a SPORT is being named.
hints.S40_C2: FIFTY LAPS EVERY MORNING is a routine, so the tense stays present, and HE is one person. Ask: does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb ending in -s? A past form would break the routine.
hints.S40_C3: LAST SPORTS DAY is finished time, and he took the ANCHOR LEG in a race that is over. Ask: which form is simple past? This verb is irregular - the vowel changes, and no -ed ending is ever allowed.
hints.S40_C4: WHILE tells you this action had already begun when THE CROWD BEGAN TO CHEER. Ask: which form shows a past action still in progress? Kai is one person, so choose the singular helper, not the plural one.
hints.S40_C5: HIS TEAMMATES is plural, and they moved ALONGSIDE HIM at the same moment, SHOUTING ENCOURAGEMENT. Ask: which form shows an action in progress in the past, and which helper matches a plural subject?
hints.S40_C6: PLANS is the deciding word: it must be followed by an infinitive, never by an -ing form. Ask: do you say 'he plans going', or 'he plans ___ go' with a small word slipped in? Supply that word here.
hints.S40_C7: SHOULD is a modal verb, and a modal always takes a bare, unchanged verb - no -s, no -ing, no infinitive marker. Ask: which box form is the plain one? EVERY ATHLETE adds nothing to it either.
hints.S40_C8: RIGHT NOW pins the action to this very moment, so it must be in progress. Ask: which form shows something happening as you read? Kai counts as one person, so take the singular helper, not 'are'.
hints.S40_D1: HUNDREDS of them LINE THE TRACK AND FIELD, CHEERING for their classes. Ask: which box word names the people who watch? It must be plural - 'hundreds of ___'. The athletes are the ones being watched.
hints.S40_D2: In the RELAY RACE, each runner must pass a METAL object TO THE NEXT TEAMMATE without dropping it. Ask: which box word names that short stick? A person or a quality cannot be passed from hand to hand.
hints.S40_D3: The gap follows ATHLETES WHO, so it must be a verb, and the events are LONG-DISTANCE contests against others. Ask: which box word means to take part in a contest? A noun cannot follow 'who' here.
hints.S40_D4: The dash defines it: KEEP GOING WHEN THEIR MUSCLES ARE TIRED and their BREATHING IS HEAVY. Ask: which box word names that staying power? It follows 'need great', so it must be a noun.
hints.S40_D5: GYMNASTIC events test MOVING QUICKLY AND GRACEFULLY through JUMPS AND ROLLS. Ask: which box word describes a body that changes direction with ease? It follows 'how', so it must be a describing word.
hints.S40_E1: THE RUNNERS is the subject - a whole line of them at the STARTING BLOCKS. Ask: does a plural subject take 'was', or its plural partner? Match the verb to the subject, not to the noun nearest the gap.
hints.S40_E2: The JUDGES did not own anything - they simply STOOD at a place NEAR THE FINISH LINE. Ask: which spelling means 'at that place'? The two words sound identical, so decide by meaning alone.
hints.S40_E3: PASSED is the action, and the underlined word describes HOW the BATON was handed over. Ask: which ending must be added before an adjective may describe an action? An adjective can only describe the baton itself.
hints.S40_E4: The NAMES belong to more than one winner, and the coach read them out over the LOUDSPEAKER. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or only number? When many people own something, where does the apostrophe land?
hints.S40_E5: RUNNED is not a word at all: this verb never takes an -ed ending. Ask: how do you say it in the past - 'yesterday she ___ home'? The vowel inside changes, exactly as swim becomes swam.
hints.S40_F1: Which half is the condition, and which is the reward? TRAIN CONSISTENTLY EVERY WEEK comes first. Ask: after 'As long as', does the verb stay simple present, or may 'will' sneak in? A comma joins the halves.
hints.S40_F2: Both halves share one subject: THE RELAY TEAM. Ask: which action came earlier - SIX MONTHS of work, or winning the DISTRICT CHAMPIONSHIP? The earlier one follows 'After', and a shared subject lets its verb change form.
